title: Your Right to a Good Faith Estimate
about: The notice 45 CFR 149.610(b)(1)(iii) requires: tells patients without insurance, or not using it, that they can get a written estimate of expected charges. Post it in the office and where visits are scheduled, and put it on the website. Adapted from CMS's model notice (CMS-10791, Appendix 1), a U.S. government work.

source.name: No Surprises Act: good faith estimates for uninsured or self-pay patients, 45 CFR 149.610

blocks.text: You have the right to a Good Faith Estimate of what your care will cost
Do you have no health insurance? Or are you not using it for this care? Then the law says we must give you an estimate of your bill before your care.

items: You can ask for a Good Faith Estimate of the total cost of your care. Ask when you schedule care, or at any time.
The estimate includes related costs, like tests, medicines, equipment and hospital fees.
Schedule care 3 or more work days ahead, and you should get the estimate in writing within 1 work day.
Schedule care 10 or more work days ahead, and you should get it within 3 work days.
Ask before you schedule, and you should get it within 3 work days.
Is your bill $400 or more above the estimate for any one provider or clinic? Then you can dispute the bill.

blocks.text: To learn more, go to the web page www.cms.gov/nosurprises/consumers. Or call 1-800-985-3059. Or email your questions to FederalPPDRQuestions@cms.hhs.gov and ask for help.
